A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a methodology for the detection, the identification and the diagnosis of process faults based on the combination of supervised and unsupervised learning techniques and the integration of the expert knowledge in the process.
the proposed methodology has been applied to a wide variety of industrial units, and that the results are encouraging in terms of the detection, diagnosis, and classification of abnormal events.
the main contribution of our research is to propose a strategy for the design and use of a tool that allows the detection of abnormal situations and the diagnosis of failures in industrial plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of a model-based approach and a data-driven approach can be used to detect anomalies in the process and to characterize them in terms of a failure mode.
the proposed strategy allows for the construction of a discrete model (states/transitions) of the process behavior from both historical and on-line data.
it has shown that a methodology based on classification methods is a promising way to build a decision support tool for process monitoring and fault diagnosis.
